name: Interview mental maths, set 4
description: Mental maths at interview speed: products, quotients, recoveries, fractions, estimates, sequences, roots, rates, coin chances and a chained battery. Each item keeps its own schedule.

items.question: What percentage gain takes it back to where it started, to the nearest percent?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Start from £100, apply the fall, then find the gain on what is left.

byKey.same: You undid a 35% fall with a 35% rise. The rise acts on the smaller value, 65, so it must be larger.
byKey.over-135: You divided by 135. After the fall the base is 65, not 135.

explain.text: After the fall, £100 is £65. Getting back needs £35 on £65, which is 35/65 ≈ 53.8%. To the nearest percent that is 54%.

items.question: Which is the middle one of 5/7, 8/11 and 13/18?

options.why: You picked the first one listed. 5/7 is 2/7 short of 1, the largest gap, so it is the smallest.
You picked the middle one listed. 8/11 is 3/11 short of 1, the smallest gap, so it is the largest.
They are close but not equal: about 0.714, 0.727 and 0.722.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare how far each fraction falls short of 1.

explain.text: Compare the gaps to 1: 2/7, 3/11 and 5/18. As decimals they are 0.286, 0.273 and 0.278. The middle gap, 5/18, belongs to 13/18, so it is the middle fraction.

items.question: What is $\sqrt{2{,}400}$ to the nearest tenth?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Start from the nearest square, 49², and take one Newton step.

byKey.rounded-down: You rounded down. 48.990 is nearer 49.0 than 48.9.
byKey.root-24: You took the root of 24. The root of 2,400 is 10 times that.
byKey.root-240: You took the root of 240. Pair the digits from the decimal point: 24 | 00.

explain.text: Start from 49² = 2,401, just 1 above 2,400. One Newton step gives 49 − 1/98 ≈ 48.990. To the nearest tenth that is 49.0.

items.prose: A tap fills a tank in 12 hours. A drain empties a full tank in 20 hours. Both are open, and the tank starts empty.
items.question: How many hours does the tank take to fill?

widget.accept: 30 hours: the net rate is 1/12 − 1/20 = 1/30 a tank an hour.
widget.label: Hours

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write each as a fraction of a tank per hour.

byKey.added: You added the two rates. The drain works against the tap, so subtract.
byKey.difference: You subtracted the times. Rates subtract, not times.
byKey.average: You averaged the times. Work with the fraction of a tank each hour instead.

explain.text: Each hour the tap adds 1/12 of a tank and the drain takes 1/20. The net is 5/60 − 3/60 = 2/60 = 1/30 of a tank an hour. So it fills in 30 hours.

items.prose: Flip a fair coin four times.
items.question: What is the chance of at least two heads? Give a fraction or a decimal.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count the outcomes with fewer than two heads and take them away.

byKey.exactly-two: You counted exactly two heads. Three and four heads count too.
byKey.at-least-one: You found the chance of at least one head. Take off the four outcomes with exactly one.
byKey.at-most-one: You found the chance of at most one head. Take it from 1.

explain.text: Of the 16 outcomes, one has no heads and four have exactly one. That leaves 16 − 5 = 11 with at least two. So the chance is 11/16 = 0.6875.

items.prose:
Work each step in your head and carry the result on.
1. Take 3/8 of 96.
2. Increase it by 25%.
3. Multiply by 16.
4. Subtract the next term of 4, 9, 16, 25.
5. Multiply by the chance that two dice show a double.
items.question: What is the result of step 5?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write each step's result down in your head before the next.

byKey.next-square-49: You took 49 as the next term. After 25 comes 36, the square of 6.
byKey.one-in-36: You used 1/36, the chance of one particular double. Six doubles give 6/36 = 1/6.
byKey.quarter-of: You took 25% of 36 instead of adding it. A rise of 25% takes 36 to 45.

explain.text: The chain runs 36, then 45, then 720, then 720 − 36 = 684. Six of the 36 rolls are doubles, a chance of 1/6. So step 5 gives 684/6 = 114.
